print(f"Number of states: {len(states_ui)}")

# Extract the values and sort in descending order
values = sorted(states_ui.values(), reverse=True)
print(f"Sorted values (descending): {values}")
print(f"Top 10 values: {values[:10]}")

# Hill estimator with k=7
# Formula: 1/alpha = (1/k) * sum(log(x_i) - log(x_{k+1})) for i = 1 to k
# where x_i are the order statistics sorted descending

k = 7
x_sorted = sorted(values, reverse=True)

# x_{k+1} is the (k+1)th largest value (index k in 0-based)
x_k_plus_1 = x_sorted[k]  # 8th largest (index 7)

print(f"\nx_{k+1} (the {k+1}th largest value): {x_k_plus_1}")

# Calculate the sum of log ratios
log_sum = 0
for i in range(k):
    xi = x_sorted[i]
    log_ratio = xi / x_k_plus_1
    print(f"i={i+1}: x_i={xi}, x_i/x_{k+1}={log_ratio:.6f}, ln={__import__('math').log(log_ratio):.6f}")
    log_sum += __import__('math').log(log_ratio)

print(f"\nSum of logs: {log_sum}")

# Hill estimator: 1/alpha = (1/k) * sum(log(x_i) - log(x_{k+1}))
hill_1_over_alpha = log_sum / k

# Tail exponent alpha
alpha = 1 / hill_1_over_alpha

print(f"\nHill estimator:")
print(f"1/alpha = {hill_1_over_alpha:.10f}")
print(f"alpha = {alpha:.10f}")
print(f"alpha rounded to nearest thousandths: {round(alpha, 3)}")
